title: React Module 01 Core Check
description: Check your understanding of React fundamentals, setup, first components, props, state, and the React mental model.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What problem does React primarily help solve?

options.text: Building user interfaces from reusable pieces of UI
Writing SQL queries in the browser
Replacing all CSS in an application

questions.explanation: React is a UI library focused on building interfaces from reusable components.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes declarative UI in React?

options.text: You manually edit DOM nodes for every change
You describe the desired UI for a given state

questions.explanation: React code describes what the UI should look like; React handles updating the DOM.

questions.prompt: Which are core React ideas introduced in this module? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Components, props, state, and composition are central React ideas. Database indexes are unrelated.

questions.prompt: In a Vite React project, which command commonly starts the development server?
questions.explanation: Vite projects commonly use `npm run dev` to start a local development server.

questions.prompt: What is the usual role of `src/main.jsx` or `src/main.tsx` in a React app?

options.text: It mounts the root React component into the HTML page

questions.explanation: The entry point creates or uses a React root and renders the app into the HTML mount point.

questions.prompt: React components should be named with a capital letter when used in JSX.
questions.explanation: Capitalized names tell JSX to treat the tag as a component instead of a built-in HTML element.

questions.prompt: What does a basic function component return?
questions.explanation: Function components return React elements, usually written with JSX.

questions.prompt: Which statements about props are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Props pass data into a component
Props should be treated as read-only by the receiving component

questions.explanation: Props are read-only inputs that configure components and can hold many value types.
